content:
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer

Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 | linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7 years of experience building and operating production services, primarily in Java and Spring. Experienced in REST API design, relational databases, event-driven systems with Kafka, automated testing, and deploying services to AWS with Docker and Kubernetes. Has improved API performance and reliability, and participates in production on-call support. Fluent in English.

WORK EXPERIENCE

Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech, Lisbon
Jan 2022 – Present
- Develop and maintain 7 Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
- Designed and versioned a REST API using OpenAPI for partner quoting integration, used by 12 broker partners.
- Produce and consume Kafka events for claims workflows; introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table, removing duplicate claim records.
- Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 ms by adding Redis caching and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
- Deploy services to Kubernetes (EKS) using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; participate in an on-call rotation one week per month.

Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A., Porto
Sep 2019 – Dec 2021
- Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
- Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, increasing payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70%.
- Contributed to splitting the monolith by extracting a notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.

Junior Developer (Internship, then full-time) | CodeFarol Lda, Porto
Jul 2018 – Aug 2019
- Maintained PHP and later Java applications for small business clients.

EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute, 2018

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java (8–17), Kotlin (basic)
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, REST, OpenAPI
Databases and caching: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis
Messaging: Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and deployment: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm
Testing and delivery: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Jenkins, Git
Other: Linux

LANGUAGES
English (fluent) | Portuguese (fluent) | Spanish (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, professional CV with clear reverse-chronological structure, relevant technical skills, and several quantified achievements. The strongest evidence includes the 75% reduction in quote-endpoint p99 latency, use by 12 broker partners, removal of duplicate claim records, and increase in test coverage from 35% to 70%. The experience bullets are specific and credible rather than responsibility-only statements. Completeness is good for the target role, although the CV could make CI/CD and query-tuning terminology more explicit for faster recruiter review.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, conventional dates, readable bullets, and no tables, graphics, columns, headers, or footers that could impair parsing. It contains strong keywords including Java, Kotlin, Spring Boot, REST, OpenAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, Docker, AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, Helm, JUnit, Testcontainers, Jenkins, and CI/CD-related delivery experience. AI screening probability is high for a comparable-language backend role, but lower for a Python-specific screen because Python, FastAPI, and GitHub Actions do not appear. Those are genuine technology gaps in the candidate information and should not be added without supporting evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the comparable-language version of the role. It demonstrates more than three years of backend development in Java, relational database experience, REST API design, Docker and AWS deployment, automated testing, Jenkins-based delivery, Kafka, Kubernetes, EKS, and production on-call support. The production-quality and dependable-services themes are supported by the API performance work, idempotent consumers, outbox pattern, and on-call rotation. The main candidate-side gaps are Python/FastAPI, explicit schema migrations, observability tooling, logistics or EDI experience, Terraform, and Dutch or French. These are not document defects and should not be represented as qualifications. The CV also does not explicitly evidence explaining technical trade-offs, blameless post-mortems, design notes, or code review, although related engineering experience is present.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/alignment enhancement:
1. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Testing and delivery" to "Automated Testing and CI/CD" and retain the existing technologies, for example: "Automated Testing and CI/CD: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Jenkins, Git." This uses the job description's terminology without adding unsupported experience.
2. In the Professional Summary, revise the sentence "Experienced in REST API design, relational databases, event-driven systems with Kafka, automated testing, and deploying services to AWS with Docker and Kubernetes" to "Experienced in designing REST APIs, relational databases, query-performance improvement, event-driven systems with Kafka, automated testing, CI/CD delivery, and deploying services to AWS with Docker and Kubernetes." The query-performance and CI/CD wording is supported by the JPA N+1 optimization, Jenkins pipelines, and testing evidence already in the CV.
3. In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, change "Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency" to "Improved quote API performance by reducing p99 latency". This makes the job's API-performance language more immediately searchable while preserving the existing quantified result.
